answer:
Use the interFoam solver as the application in system/controlDict.
The computational domain is 10 m in the x-direction by 1 m in the y-direction, extruded one cell in the z-direction.
The mesh is a 2D blockMesh with 100 cells in x, 10 cells in y, and 1 cell in z.
The frontAndBack patch boundary condition is set to empty.
The bottom boundary (y = 0) is a noSlip wall.
The left boundary (x = 0) is a noSlip wall representing the dam face.
The right boundary (x = 10 m) uses inletOutlet for pressure and velocity to allow outflow.
The top boundary (y = 1 m) uses inletOutlet for pressure and velocity to allow air exchange.
Gravity is set to (0 -9.81 0) m/s^2 in constant/g.
Water properties: rho0 = 1000 kg/m^3, nu = 1e-6 m^2/s.
Air properties: rho0 = 1.2 kg/m^3, nu = 1.8e-5 m^2/s.
Surface tension coefficient sigma is 0.07 N/m.
A setFields dictionary is provided that sets alpha.water = 1 in the region x from 0 to 5 m and y from 0 to 1 m, and alpha.water = 0 everywhere else.
The initial velocity field U is zero everywhere.
The time step starts at 0.001 s with maxCo = 1 and maxDeltaT = 0.01 s.
The free surface is captured sharply using the MULES compression scheme built into interFoam.
